style.vernacular: Dense Pacific-side skyline of glass and white-concrete towers (Punta Pacifica, Costa del Este, Avenida Balboa) beside the pastel colonial and French/Antillean townhouses of Casco Viejo with wrought-iron balconies and clay-tile or zinc roofs; mid-century Canal Zone and 1970s civic blocks are low, flat-roofed, cream or white painted concrete with louvred openings; older El Chorrillo houses are timber-framed, and everything sits under strong tropical rain and cloud with royal palms and broadleaf trees.
style.ornament: Casco Viejo wrought-iron balconies and louvred timber shutters, calicanto (lime, stone and brick) walls, arcaded ground-floor portales, French and Antillean timber verandas; baroque curved gables and mother-of-pearl inlaid belfries on colonial churches; neoclassical Ionic columns on early-1900s civic buildings; louvres and brise-soleil on modern blocks.

sources.what: Casco Viejo mixes Spanish colonial, French, Antillean, Republican and art deco styles (~800 buildings); dense high-rise skyline (127 completed high-rises); calicanto walls; timber-framed El Chorrillo; tropical savanna climate
colonial cathedral: stone facade, towers with mother-of-pearl inlay, white interior, gabled roof
baroque colonial church, masonry walls, corrugated zinc roof replacing tiles in 1911
